question: Should OpenClaw adopt YAML-frontmatter `CLAW.md` as the canonical human-authored and exported Claw manifest while retaining JSON as a read-compatible legacy representation?
rationale: The implementation can establish parsing correctness, but choosing the durable package representation and stacked landing order is a public format decision that automation cannot make safely.

options.title: Resolve RFC and stack first
options.body: Keep this PR open as a draft until the RFC direction and prerequisite lifecycle contracts are approved, then land it as the canonical representation slice.

options.title: Approve CLAW.md now
options.body: Explicitly accept `CLAW.md` as canonical and queue this PR behind the prerequisite stack with the documented JSON read-compatibility boundary.

options.title: Keep JSON canonical
options.body: Retain JSON as the exported default and narrow this PR to optional `CLAW.md` reading until a later format decision.

recommendation.title: Resolve RFC and stack first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open as a draft until the RFC direction and prerequisite lifecycle contracts are approved, then land it as the canonical representation slice.
